name: TenPrint

overview.text: The rubric-protocol.com homepage presents TenPrint AI decision/session evidence while documentation retains Rubric Protocol naming. It describes ML-DSA-65 signatures, Merkle batching and Hedera anchors. An immediate ID/local signed leaf is not a confirmed anchor; unkeyed local attestations are not automatically HCS-anchored. Hedera is the sole active anchor, with Base paused. Homepage session plans list 1,000 free anchored sessions/month, $29/month encrypted escrow for one year, $349 for seven years and $0.05 per wallet-paid retained session. Documentation separately lists $0.005 x402 tiered attestations, not the same unit. Enterprise prices conflict: $2,500/month after a 60-day pilot versus FAQ from $999. Direct attestation is Enterprise-only, tiered supports Developer, and the old batch route is unavailable. Five nodes/three signatures do not establish independent operators. Hash-only language does not exclude encrypted payload storage in escrow/tiered routes with customer-held keys. Integrity/inclusion does not prove correctness, fairness, compliance or admissibility; performance, post-quantum and retention/destruction claims are not independent audits.

disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (23:09-23:11 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with TenPrint or YourAITools is involved.
